text:
cust-jones: Hey @support-ops — urgent compliance question. We set a custom retention window (policy id policy-14d) for a subset of records in workspace org-777 to 14d, but our export for this workspace still shows those records as present after 21 days. Default retention is 90d for the rest of the workspace. Also we rotated our KMS key last Thursday (alias/aws/redwood-org-777). Could rotation have prevented deletion/decryption for the export? This is blocking an external audit.

support-ops: Hi, sorry for the trouble — we'll escalate. Can you share the policy id and a sample record_id and the approximate deletion timestamp? Also any error IDs from the export job would help.

cust-jones: policy id is policy-14d, sample record_id rec-42, deletion API call returned 200 at 2026-09-03T15:22:11Z. Export job id from the console: export-20260904-83. No errors in the UI. Attached minimal repro:
```
POST /v1/records/delete
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
{ "workspace": "org-777", "record_id": "rec-42" }
```
response: 200 { "status": "scheduled_for_deletion", "ttl": "14d" }

sam-ritchie: looping in @security-eng and @anika. Can you check KMS/HSM logs for key material usage around that deletion time? :eyes:

security-eng: quick note: KMS key rotation can affect our ability to decrypt older ciphertext only if the service attempted to re-encrypt with a new key and the old key was destroyed outside of KMS's scheduled key rotation policy. Our typical flow keeps ciphertext verifiable for 30d after rotation. Do you have the KMS key version/arn?

cust-jones: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-1234 (rotated -> version 2 on 2026-09-02). We use customer-managed CMKs.

anika: checking audit logs now. @audit-bot can you run an export of audit entries for workspace org-777 between 2026-08-30 and 2026-09-05 and include delete events for rec-42?

audit-bot: export job audit-export-1830009 queued. Status: running.

support-ops: while we wait for the audit export, couple of quick checks that help root cause: 1) Confirm the delete API actually wrote a tombstone (we store tombstones for custom-retention deletions). 2) Confirm export pipeline ran after tombstone created (there's a timing window). 3) Provide the raw export JSON you downloaded (if possible).

cust-jones: I only have the S3 bundle we downloaded from console export-20260904-83 — I can upload a redacted copy. Also, the delete API response included ttl 14d and operation_id op-9f8.

audit-bot: audit-export-1830009 completed. attachment: audit-export-org-777-20260904.json (contains event: {"type":"delete","record_id":"rec-42","actor":"api:user-cj","ts":"2026-09-03T15:22:11Z","policy":"policy-14d"}).

security-eng: audit shows deletion event present. That means the application accepted the delete and wrote tombstone. Two probable causes: 1) Export pipeline filter mis-applied and excluded tombstones for custom-retention records. 2) Decryption failure during export step for objects encrypted under the old key version — export silently skipped the object (we should have surfaced errors, so that's suspicious).

support-ops: can you run this internal diagnostic (if you have an engineer):
```
# check export job logs
GET https://internal.redwood/api/v1/internal/exports/export-20260904-83/logs
# fetch object from S3 and attempt decryption with service key ring (internal only)
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-exports/org-777/export-20260904-83/objects/rec-42.json - | jq .
```
If you prefer, we can run this from our side — just tell us to proceed and grant a one-time support access window.

cust-jones: please run it from your side, we'll grant access for a 2h window. We're worried about audit evidence. Also noted we saw a small billing spike around 2026-09-04 due to repeated export retries. Can you confirm retries were exponential backoff or a bug?

sam-ritchie: noted, @support-ops proceed with access, I'll attach the temporary SSO link. Also @finance FYI re billing spike.

support-ops: starting diagnostic run now. First look: export logs show a handful of "decryption_error" entries around 2026-09-03T15:22:xx for objects encrypted with key id abcd-1234:v1. There is a follow-up error that should have been escalated but wasn't due to a log sampling rule. Captured sample: 
```
ERROR decryption_error object=rec-42 key=arn:aws:kms:...:key/abcd-1234:1 cause=AccessDenied
```

security-eng: that AccessDenied indicates the service principal didn't have permissions on the old key version after rotation. For CMKs, rotating the key should preserve aliases, but customer-managed policies can restrict older key usage. If the customer disabled key version 1, decrypts fail. We need to verify policy changes in the KMS key history.

cust-jones: we did update the KMS key policy on 2026-09-02 to limit usage to a narrower role as part of internal rotation. We didn't realize it would affect exports. That was the change.

anika: ok that explains missing items in S3 export. Action items: 1) security-eng will help guide temporary re-grant of decrypt permission to Redwood service principal for key:v1 (or re-encrypt objects to new key) so we can complete an accurate export for audit. 2) support-ops will regenerate the export after decryption succeeds and confirm rec-42 tombstone is present in S3 bundle. 3) finance will review spike and credit any repeat-export cost attributable to this issue. 4) we will add an alert on decryption_error sampling so it doesn't get missed.

support-ops: provisional timeline — we can do the re-check and re-export within 2-4 hours once permissions restored. If you want immediate evidence for audit, we can provide the audit-export JSON (it contains the delete event) as provisional proof while we fix the export pipeline.

cust-jones: please do both — we need the audit-export JSON now and the corrected S3 bundle after. Also please document the deletion timeline for auditors: when API call occurred, when tombstone written, when export ran and when we will re-run it after permission change.

security-eng: under action items. For long-term, we'll add a KMS rotation playbook to call out that CMK policy changes can impact exports and to include a post-rotation validation step (decrypt a sample blob).

support-ops: thanks — opening internal ticket RDW-4572 and legal hold flagging. Closing loop: cust-jones, I'll DM for the temporary support access (SSO link) and send the audit-export JSON attachment to your compliance mailbox. :lock:

cust-jones: appreciated, thanks everyone.
